grammar.q: She ___ my big sister.
grammar.why: Use 'is' with he, she and it.

grammar.q: My grandma and grandpa ___ very kind.
grammar.why: Use 'are' for two or more people (they).

grammar.q: I ___ got two brothers.
grammar.why: Say 'I have got', but 'he has got' and 'she has got'.

grammar.q: My dad ___ got a big red car.
grammar.why: My dad = he. Use 'has got' with he, she and it.

grammar.q: ___ is that girl? She's my sister.
grammar.why: Use 'who' to ask about a person.

grammar.q: ___ old is your brother? He's ten.
grammar.why: Ask 'How old...?' to find out someone's age.

grammar.q: I ___ seven years old.
grammar.why: Use 'am' with I: I am seven.

grammar.q: This is my cousin. ___ name is Ana.
grammar.why: Ana is a girl, so use 'her': her name is Ana.

grammar.q: ___ your sister got a bike? Yes, she has.
grammar.why: Ask 'Has he got...?' or 'Has she got...?' about one person.

grammar.q: My grandma ___ young. She is old.
grammar.why: Use 'isn't' (is not) with he, she and it.

sentences: My grandmother has got white hair.
How old is your sister?
My baby sister is one year old.
Happy birthday to my mum!
Who is the girl in this photo?
My grandpa has got new glasses.

reading.title: Meet Lily's family
reading.text: Hello! My name is Lily and I am eight. This is my family. My mother is a teacher and my father is a doctor. I have got one brother. His name is Max and he is five. We have got a grandmother too. She lives with us and she makes great cakes. We are a happy family!

reading.title: A family photo
reading.text: Look at my family photo! This is me. My name is Ana and I am seven. The tall man is my dad and the woman next to him is my mum. The boy with glasses is my cousin Leo. He is nine. My little sister is sad in the photo because she wants her teddy bear!

qs.q: The woman next to Ana's dad is her mum.
What does Ana's little sister want?

grammar.q: Can a bird fly? Yes, it ___.
grammar.why: Answer a 'Can...?' question with 'can': Yes, it can. Or: No, it can't.

grammar.q: A snake ___ walk. It has got no legs.
grammar.why: 'Can't' means it is not able to. A snake has no legs, so it can't walk.

grammar.q: I can see ___ elephant.
grammar.why: Use 'an' before words that start with a, e, i, o or u: an elephant.

grammar.q: Look! There's ___ duck on the water.
grammar.why: Use 'a' before most words, like 'a duck'. Use 'an' before a, e, i, o and u.

grammar.q: Grandma has got three ___.
grammar.why: For more than one, add -s: one cat, three cats.

grammar.q: Look at those two ___!
grammar.why: Some words change: one mouse, two mice.

grammar.q: Look at the three ___! They say 'baa'.
grammar.why: Some words don't change: one sheep, three sheep.

grammar.q: ___ a lion swim? Yes, it can.
grammar.why: Ask with 'Can': Can a lion swim? Yes, it can.

grammar.q: A spider ___ got eight legs.
grammar.why: A spider = it. Use 'has got' with he, she and it.

grammar.q: What ___ these? They're crocodiles.
grammar.why: 'These' means more than one thing, so ask 'What are these?'

A frog can jump very well.
My cat has got a long tail.
The giraffe is very tall.
A spider has got eight legs.
The hippo is swimming in the river.

reading.title: At the zoo
reading.text: Today Sam is at the zoo with his dad. He can see two elephants. They are big and grey. A monkey is eating a banana in a tree. Sam likes the giraffes. They are very tall! There is a snake too, but Sam doesn't like it. It is long and green.

qs.q: How many elephants can Sam see?

reading.title: On Grandpa's farm
reading.text: My grandpa has got a farm. There are four cows and twenty sheep. The cows are black and white. There is a big brown horse too, and I can ride it! Grandpa's dog runs after the sheep. It is very fast. I love Grandpa's farm!

qs.q: The writer can ride the horse.

grammar.q: Can I have ___ apple, please?
grammar.why: 'Apple' starts with 'a', so use 'an': an apple.

grammar.q: There ___ two eggs on the table.
grammar.why: Use 'there are' for more than one thing: there are two eggs.

grammar.q: There ___ a cake in the kitchen.
grammar.why: Use 'there is' for one thing: there is a cake.

grammar.q: ___ is your favourite food? Pizza!
grammar.why: Use 'what' to ask about a thing.

grammar.q: We ___ got three bananas.
grammar.why: Use 'have got' with I, you, we and they.

grammar.q: ___ your milk, please.
grammar.why: To tell someone to do something, use the verb on its own: Drink your milk.

grammar.q: I like grapes, but I ___ like lemons.
grammar.why: Say 'I don't like' for things you do not like.

grammar.q: ___ you like chocolate? Yes, I do!
grammar.why: Ask 'Do you like...?' and answer 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'.

grammar.q: Can I have two ___, please?

sentences: Can I have an apple, please?
My brother doesn't like carrots.
This ice cream is very cold.
What is your favourite food?

I don't like lemons very much.

reading.title: Ben loves food
reading.text: My name is Ben and I love food! For breakfast I eat bread and an egg, and I drink orange juice. At lunch I eat chicken and rice. My favourite food is pizza with tomatoes. I don't like carrots, but my sister loves them. After dinner we have ice cream. Yum!

qs.q: What does Ben drink for breakfast?
When do they have ice cream?

reading.title: A picnic in the park
reading.text: It is Sunday and we are in the park with Mum and Dad. We have got a big picnic! There are sandwiches, grapes and a big green watermelon. My brother Tim loves burgers, but we haven't got burgers today. He is sad. Then Mum gives him a big piece of chocolate cake. Now he is happy!

qs.q: At the end, Tim is happy.

grammar.q: There are three pictures ___ the wall.
grammar.why: Use 'on' when a thing touches the top or side of something: on the wall.

grammar.q: My shoes are ___ my bed, on the floor.
grammar.why: 'Under' means below something: the shoes are on the floor below the bed.

grammar.q: The sweets are ___ the box. Open it and take one!
grammar.why: 'In' means inside something. You open the box to get them.

grammar.q: There ___ three bedrooms in our house.
grammar.why: Use 'there are' for more than one thing.

grammar.q: ___ there a garden? Yes, there is.
grammar.why: Ask 'Is there...?' about one thing.

grammar.q: Please ___ the window. It's cold.
grammar.why: To tell someone to do something, use the verb on its own: close.

grammar.q: ___ there two bathrooms in your house? Yes, there are.
grammar.why: Ask 'Are there...?' about more than one thing.

grammar.q: Where ___ my shoes? They're under the bed.
grammar.why: 'Shoes' means more than one, so use 'are': Where are my shoes?

grammar.q: Don't ___ on the sofa!
grammar.why: Use 'Don't' + the verb on its own to tell someone not to do something.

grammar.q: Put the plates ___ the cupboard and close the door.
grammar.why: 'In' means inside. The plates go inside the cupboard, and then you close the door.

Don't open the kitchen window.
How many rooms are there in your house?

We live in a big flat.

reading.title: My home
reading.text: This is my home. It is a small house with a big garden. There are two bedrooms. My bedroom is blue. My bed is next to the window. The kitchen is yellow and there is a big table in it. We have got a red sofa in the living room. My cat sleeps on it every day!

qs.q: The house has got a small garden.
The bed is next to the window.

reading.title: Zoe's flat
reading.text: Zoe lives in a flat in a tall building. It has got a small kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms. In the living room there is a green sofa and a big lamp. There is a clock on the wall. Zoe's bedroom has got a cupboard for her toys. From her window she can see the park.

qs.q: The clock is on the wall.
Zoe's flat has got three bedrooms.
What can Zoe see from her window?

reading.title: Kim's toy box
reading.text: Hi! I'm Kim. I have got a big toy box in my bedroom. In my toy box there are ten balls. Three are red and seven are blue. There is a green robot and a yellow train. My favourite toy is my teddy bear. He is brown and his name is Bobby.

qs.q: How many balls are in the toy box?

reading.title: Jack's birthday toys
reading.text: It's Jack's birthday. He is eight. He has got lots of new toys! His grandma gives him a black and white football. His cousin gives him a purple kite. From Mum and Dad he gets an orange bike. He can't ride it very well, but he is very happy!

qs.q: Jack can ride his bike very well.

reading.title: A sunny day in the park
reading.text: It is a sunny day and Lucy is at the park with her dad. There are lots of flowers and big green trees. Lucy can't swim, but she can ride her bike. Her dad is reading under a tree. Two boys are playing baseball. Lucy waves to them and smiles.

qs.q: What are the two boys playing?

reading.title: Tom's picnic
reading.text: Tom and his family are having a picnic in the park. They sit on the grass next to the water. There are three boats on the water: a red boat, a blue boat and a yellow boat. Tom's sister is in the playground. She is playing in the sand. Tom wants to play badminton with Mum.

qs.q: There is a green boat on the water.
Tom wants to play badminton with Mum.
